A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical study of equivariant ReLU networks. Their text, equations, two figures and Appendices A-G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical proofs and constructive examples, including plots of analytically defined functions. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v3 retains the theoretical study and illustrative function plots. No experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis results are introduced, including in the appendices.

M1.justification: The two-layer ReLU formulations, group-averaging construction, channel-orbit merging and multilayer construction in Appendix E remain unchanged. Reworded explanations and corrected matrix dimensions do not establish an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or application tasks. Example 5.1 retains the same invariant target function on R2; the additional application domains mentioned in v3 concern related literature.

E2.justification: The theoretical comparisons still concern GNs, GENs and LENs. Neither version evaluates empirical baselines; newly cited methods provide context or attribution.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental protocol. The squared-error criterion and fixed-width theoretical comparisons remain. v3's explicit statement about matching architecture and model size clarifies these comparisons without introducing an evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness, sensitivity or error-analysis experiments appear in either version. The constructive counterexample and parameter-count example are retained; condensing their overlapping exposition does not remove a distinct analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. The numerical examples retain the three-versus-six neuron comparison and five-versus-nine parameter counts. The mathematical correction and reinterpretation of those counts are assessed under T1 and C2.

T1.justification: Section 6.1 corrects v1's reversed relation between boundary-hyperplane and channel counts: v3 states that a GEN with k boundary hyperplanes can be represented using k+2 channels. Section 6.3 also replaces asserted hypothesis-space dimensions with parameter-space dimensions. The principal theorem statements and proofs in Appendices A-G are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims remain expressivity loss under equivariance constraints, compensation through model enlargement, and a potential complexity/generalization advantage. v3 highlights enlargement bounds in the abstract and conclusion, but these bounds were already central contributions in v1.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 changes the interpretation of five versus nine from hypothesis-space dimensions to parameter counts and parameter spaces R5 and R9. Section 6.2 explicitly qualifies its compression discussion as targeting invariant functions. The broader generalization interpretation remains.

D1.justification: The explicit theoretical weight constructions are retained. Neither version supplies experimental implementation settings, hardware information or code/data access instructions; v3's added review link does not provide reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands related work and revises attribution of central results. Lemma 4.4 now credits Godfrey et al. (2022) and Bökman and Kahl (2023), Theorem 6.3 credits Elesedy and Zaidi (2021), and Section 6.1 acknowledges that Theorem 6.2 follows alternatively from Agrawal and Ostrowski (2022). It positions the retained proof's geometric perspective against that prior result and adds discussion of approximate equivariance.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, related work, problem formulation, explanatory passages and conclusion. Subsection headings are revised and redundant parameter-count exposition is condensed. The overall section sequence and Appendices A-G remain.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2, their plots and captions are unchanged, and neither version contains tables. v3 adds publication headers and review front matter, adjusts spacing and page breaks, and reformats long equations in Appendix E.

improvement.justification: v3 improves scholarly attribution around Lemma 4.4 and Theorems 6.2-6.3, corrects the channel-count relation in Section 6.1, and more accurately describes the parameter counts in Section 6.3. These changes improve precision and positioning. The central proofs remain essentially unchanged, and the generalization advantage remains an inference from complexity arguments, so the overall improvement is limited.
